rules.name: HTTP request inside loop
rules.description: Detects unbatched network and HTTP calls in loops.

rules.name: String concatenation in loop
rules.description: Detects repeated string concatenation in loops causing O(n^2) reallocation.

rules.name: File I/O inside loop
rules.description: Detects repetitive file open and read/write operations inside loops.

rules.name: Uncompiled regex inside loop
rules.description: Detects direct re.search/match calls inside loops.

rules.name: Linear search inside loop
rules.description: Detects linear membership testing (x in list) inside loops causing quadratic behavior.

rules.name: Synchronous blocking I/O in async function
rules.description: Detects synchronous blocking operations (time.sleep, open, requests) inside async coroutines that block the event loop.

rules.name: Deepcopy inside loop
rules.description: Detects copy.deepcopy calls inside loops causing extensive object traversal and allocation overhead.

rules.name: Sorting inside loop
rules.description: Detects sorted() or list.sort() calls inside loops causing O(n * m log m) complexity.

rules.name: Redundant comprehension or conversion call
rules.description: Detects redundant wrapping of list/set/dict comprehensions or generator expressions in list(), set(), or dict() calls.

rules.name: Unnecessary dict.keys() iteration or membership check
rules.description: Detects redundant .keys() calls in 'for ... in d.keys()' and 'x in d.keys()' membership tests.

rules.name: Unnecessary len() call in boolean context
rules.description: Detects len(x) > 0, len(x) == 0, and len(x) != 0 in conditions; truthiness checks (if x:, if not x:) are more idiomatic and faster.

rules.name: math.pow() or pow() in loop instead of multiplication operator
rules.description: Detects math.pow(x, 2) or pow(x, 2) in loops; x * x executes 3-5x faster in tight numerical loops.

rules.name: Double dictionary lookup instead of dict.get()
rules.description: Detects 'if k in d: v = d[k] else: v = default' pattern; dict.get() performs a single hash lookup instead of two.

rules.name: Mutable default argument in function definition
rules.description: Detects mutable default arguments ([], {}, set()) in function definitions; defaults are instantiated once at module load, leading to state leaks across calls.

rules.name: Manual loop append instead of list.extend()
rules.description: Detects 'for item in seq: out.append(item)'; list.extend() performs a single pre-allocation in C and executes 2-4x faster.

rules.name: Resource opened without context manager
rules.description: Detects open() calls outside of 'with' statements, risking unclosed file descriptors and deferred garbage collection stalls.

rules.name: Eager list comprehension in any() or all() short-circuiting call
rules.description: Detects any([x for x in seq]) and all([x for x in seq]); eagerly allocating a list prevents short-circuiting and wastes memory.

rules.name: sorted()[0] or sorted()[-1] instead of min() or max()
rules.description: Detects sorted(seq)[0] or sorted(seq)[-1]; min() and max() run in linear O(n) time and O(1) space instead of O(n log n) sort.

rules.name: Unnecessary list comprehension passed to iterable consumer
rules.description: Detects sum([...]) and tuple([...]); passing generator expression avoids intermediate list allocation.

rules.name: Membership test against list literal instead of set
rules.description: Detects `x in [...]` or `x not in [...]`; list literals allocate a new list heap object on every evaluation and perform O(n) search. Using a set literal `{...}` compiles to a constant frozenset with O(1) lookup.

rules.name: Unnecessary lambda wrapping single function call
rules.description: Detects `lambda x: f(x)` wrappers; passing `f` directly avoids extra Python call frame allocation and function invocation overhead.

rules.name: Redundant None default in dict.get()
rules.description: Detects `dict.get(key, None)`; None is already the default return value for dict.get(), so passing None explicitly is redundant.

rules.name: Unnecessary async def coroutine
rules.description: Detects `async def` coroutines containing no await/async with/async for expressions, which incur coroutine allocation and event loop overhead.

rules.name: Unused index in enumerate() loop
rules.description: Detects `for idx, item in enumerate(...)` where `idx` is never referenced, incurring unnecessary tuple construction and counter tracking.

rules.name: Unused value in dict.items() iteration
rules.description: Detects `for key, value in d.items()` loops where `value` is unused, incurring unnecessary 2-tuple allocations on every iteration.

rules.name: Dict comprehension duplicating dict.items()
rules.description: Detects `{k: v for k, v in d.items()}` which can be replaced with `d.copy()`, avoiding Python loop overhead and running ~8.5x faster.

rules.name: Redundant nested collection constructor call
rules.description: Detects redundant nested collection calls like `list(list(x))` or `set(set(x))` that allocate redundant intermediate memory.

rules.name: Redundant f-string with no formatted expressions
rules.description: Detects f-strings that contain no interpolated expressions and can be written as plain string literals.

rules.name: Multiple startswith() or endswith() calls can use tuple argument
rules.description: Detects multiple startswith() or endswith() calls on the same string joined with 'or' and suggests combining them into a single call with a tuple.

rules.name: Dictionary comprehension with constant value can use dict.fromkeys()
rules.description: Detects dictionary comprehensions of the form '{k: <constant> for k in keys}' and suggests 'dict.fromkeys(keys, <constant>)' for faster C-level hash table allocation.

rules.name: itertools.chain(*iterables) can use itertools.chain.from_iterable()
rules.description: Detects 'itertools.chain(*iterables)' unpacking an iterable and suggests 'itertools.chain.from_iterable(iterables)' to avoid argument tuple allocation.

rules.name: try-except KeyError instead of dict.get()
rules.description: Detects 'try: var = d[k] except KeyError: var = default' patterns and suggests 'd.get(k, default)' to eliminate expensive exception handling.

rules.name: try-except KeyError around dict.pop() instead of default argument
rules.description: Detects 'try: d.pop(k) except KeyError: pass' or assignment fallback and suggests 'd.pop(k, default)'.

rules.name: Empty if-pass-else branch can invert condition
rules.description: Detects 'if condition: pass else: body' and suggests inverting the condition to eliminate the empty branch and jump opcodes.

rules.name: Multiple isinstance() checks can use tuple argument
rules.description: Detects multiple isinstance(x, T) checks on the same target chained with 'or' and suggests combining them into isinstance(x, (T1, T2)).

rules.name: Slicing list() or tuple() of iterable instead of itertools.islice()
rules.description: Detects list(seq)[:n] and tuple(seq)[:n] patterns that realize entire sequences in memory before slicing; itertools.islice() consumes lazily with O(1) allocation.

rules.name: re.sub() with literal string pattern instead of str.replace()
rules.description: Detects re.sub() calls with literal patterns and replacements lacking regex metacharacters; str.replace() bypasses the regex engine and runs 3x faster.

rules.name: Manual prefix or suffix slicing instead of removeprefix/removesuffix
rules.description: Detects 'if s.startswith(p): s = s[len(p):]' or 'if s.endswith(suf): s = s[:-len(suf)]' and suggests s.removeprefix(p) or s.removesuffix(suf).

rules.name: math.log() with base 2 or 10 instead of math.log2() or math.log10()
rules.description: Detects math.log(x, 2) and math.log(x, 10) calls; specialized math.log2() and math.log10() use direct C/FPU instructions, running 2x faster.

rules.name: try-except StopIteration around next() instead of default argument
rules.description: Detects 'try: v = next(it) except StopIteration: v = default' and suggests 'v = next(it, default)' to avoid exception frame unwinding.

rules.name: Unbounded string split before indexing
rules.description: Detects s.split(...)[0] or s.rsplit(...)[-1] without maxsplit; supplying maxsplit avoids allocating and traversing a list of all tokens.

rules.name: Comprehension truthiness filtering instead of filter(None, ...)
rules.description: Detects [x for x in seq if x]; list(filter(None, seq)) executes truthiness filtering in C with 1.5x speedup and lower memory overhead.

rules.name: Membership iteration in all() instead of set.issuperset()
rules.description: Detects all(x in b for x in a); set(b).issuperset(a) is up to 3.5x faster, avoiding bytecode iteration and generator framing.
